# Atrial Fibrillation

This folder contains the specific clinical quality indicators and development targets used to monitor the treatment, safety, and outcomes of patients with atrial fibrillation in Denmark. It tracks anticoagulation treatment persistence at one, two, and five years post-diagnosis, the incidence of major bleeding events to assess pharmacological safety, and the provision of structured patient education programs. Additionally, it defines the normative benchmarks—such as the ≥90% development target for treatment coverage and the strict ≤0.6% threshold for intracranial bleeding—against which national, regional, and local healthcare performance is evaluated.

## Pages

- [[indikator-4a1|Indikator 4a1]] — Measures the proportion of eligible atrial fibrillation patients receiving anticoagulation one year post-diagnosis, with a national standard of ≥90%.
- [[indikator-4a2|Indikator 4a2]] — Tracks sustained anticoagulation coverage two years after the index date to evaluate long-term guideline adherence.
- [[indikator-4a3|Indikator 4a3]] — Evaluates five-year treatment persistence for anticoagulation, highlighting geographic variations in long-term cardiovascular care.
- [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] — Surveils the incidence of major bleeding among prevalent patients using adapted ISTH criteria to evaluate the safety of anticoagulant therapies.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Assesses the provision of structured patient education within the first year of diagnosis, relying on specific SKS coding (BFKB) for target fulfillment.
- [[udviklingsmaal-90-percent|"Udviklingsmål ≥ 90%"]] — Establishes the standardized quality benchmark mandating that at least 90% of specific patient cohorts receive guideline-recommended care.
- [[udviklingsmaal|Udviklingsmål]] — Defines the normative standard for Indicator 6, setting the maximum acceptable incidence of intracranial bleeding at ≤0.6%.
